readings: Group the income records by linked member (`income.link_to_member`), after first dropping every income record whose `link_to_member` is missing, so such income plays no part in anything below. Sum `amount` in each group. Each group's share is its sum divided by the sum of all the group sums; then take the plain average of the shares across groups. Keep only groups whose share is strictly greater than that average, and return one row with: (1) the total of their summed amounts, (2) the average of their shares, and (3) the average of (share minus average share). Do not round.
queries:
WITH member_totals AS (
    SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) AS member_amount
    FROM income
    WHERE link_to_member IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY link_to_member
),
shares AS (
    SELECT
        member_amount,
        1.0 * member_amount / SUM(member_amount) OVER () AS share
    FROM member_totals
),
benchmark AS (
    SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share
    FROM shares
)
SELECT
    SUM(shares.member_amount),
    AVG(shares.share),
    AVG(shares.share - benchmark.average_share)
FROM shares
CROSS JOIN benchmark
WHERE shares.share > benchmark.average_share
